value.rationale: The source highlights persistent-memory advantage under noise but proves reliable decoding only below p<1/16. The new theorem identifies a qualitatively different, full nontrivial BSC regime in which one register pair already preserves positive exact-message success while every same-resource classical-memory QC receiver vanishes. The explicit limit and sharp p=1/2 endpoint quantify how that advantage degrades and separate nonvanishing decoding from the stronger reliability threshold.
